_comment: TEMPLATE ONLY. Copy to config/live_operation.json (gitignored) to authorize live multi-model operation. The real file is DELIBERATELY absent from the repo: a fresh clone is DENIED-by-absence (directive s10.1). Under OP-6 (directive s11) the loop itself MAY create/maintain the real file. Scope is fixed by the operator ruling and cannot be widened here. The config cites exactly ONE authorizing register row and receives exactly that row's provider set: OP-6 => claude_code + openai_codex_cli (the operator/directive shorthand 'codex' normalizes to the frozen node.schema.json adapter id openai_codex_cli); OP-12 => those two PLUS grok_build (CLI 'grok') and google_antigravity (CLI 'agy'). Naming a Grok/Antigravity provider under row OP-6 fails closed - rows do not lend each other scope. A config may NARROW (fewer providers, 1 terminal) but any widening fails closed (the loader raises).
_comment_terminals: terminals_per_subscription is the GLOBAL ceiling (1..2). Each provider is further capped in code, so grok_build and google_antigravity are 1 each even under the value below - OP-12 s12: separate subscription resources grok_build_subscription and google_antigravity_subscription, never merged, raised only by a separate operator amendment. There is deliberately NO shorthand for the new providers: 'gemini' is ambiguous (node@1.0 carries a different member spelled gemini_cli, the retired personal-account CLI) and 'grok' is a runner parameter spelling, not an identity.
_comment_u227: RULED by the operator on 2026-08-01 (OP-12.1, directive s17.1), and this comment said the opposite for one commit. It read: 'OPEN, operator-reserved: neither grok_build nor google_antigravity is a member of the frozen node@1.0 adapter enum, so no schema-valid node RECORD can name them ... the canonical node-record vocabulary is unchanged, and NodeRegistry.register refuses any adapter outside it.' All three clauses are now false. The resolution was a SUCCESSOR schema: schemas/node.schema@1.1.json carries the frozen eight PLUS grok_build, google_antigravity and ollama_local (the 15E product-layer drift, U254, admitted by the same ruling); node@1.0 is byte-unchanged and still frozen; NodeRegistry.register's vocabulary is the UNION over the schema versions, derived from the files. What that does NOT mean: no node record for either provider EXISTS, because nothing is wired to create one yet.
_comment_effect: READ THIS BEFORE COPYING. Naming the OP-12 pair here is NOT inert. Since 18B .picker the pane picker OFFERS both providers, the pane authorizer DISPATCHES them, and the runner status surface reports both REGISTERED - so this edit makes grok_build and google_antigravity selectable, spawnable, and lease-taking (1 terminal each, never merged, never raised without a new operator amendment). An earlier version of this comment said 'selecting either is not possible today' - true when it was written at 18B .scope, falsified by .picker, and corrected here at the 18B close because this is the file the operator reads while deciding (invariant 1: final authority has to be INFORMED authority). What copying this template still does NOT do: it cannot widen the code-pinned scope, it registers no Sovereign node for either provider (the vocabulary admits one since OP-12.1 - see _comment_u227 - but no code path creates one), and no live call happens until a pane is actually launched.
